newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Gov taps Long Island developer to LIPA board.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Gov taps Long Island developer to LIPA board.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki, who has proposed a partial state takeover of the Long Island Lighting Co, on Thursday appointed a lawyer and local homebuilder to the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA).

Robert McMillan, the founder and chairman of Long Island Housing Partnership, which Pataki said was one of the largest homebuilders on the island, was tapped to be a board member. LIPA is slated to conduct the partial takeover of the lighting company.

The Authority's newest board member also is a partner with the law firm of McMillan, Rather, Bennett & Rigano, P.C., and his background includes serving as an Honor Graduate Attorney in the U.S. anti-trust division, Pataki noted, in prepared remarks.
McMillan, who in 1989 was named by former President George Bush to the Panama Canal Commission, was elected chairman of the commission in October 1993, and served in that post through October 1994.
